text:
Marathon Petroleum rose 1.9% today, continuing a strong two-week rally that's added 9% to the stock price. The immediate driver appears to be oil market dynamics: U.S. crude is trading at $107 per barrel while global crude sits at $130.80, creating a significant price gap that typically benefits refiners who buy cheaper domestic oil and sell refined products into higher-priced global markets. Refineries are running at 96.8% capacity, near maximum utilization, which means the company is maximizing profit from that spread.

The broader context here is that oil prices have been volatile but supported. Though crude fell earlier this week on Saudi Arabia's pledges to increase supply, prices remain elevated—well above $100 domestically and $130 globally—which keeps refining margins attractive. The two-week climb in MPC's stock reflects this refiner-friendly environment where high global oil prices and tight capacity utilization combine to boost profitability.
